legacy.statement: Inventory located the six paths only. All source evidence below is from this recovery's actual read calls and independent before/after metadata. Original transport-04 reports were not modified.

method.lineConvention: rawLines = UTF-8 ReadAllLines physical lines, final newline does not add an extra empty line; nonBlankLines = Trim().Length > 0. Metadata reads are not semantic read proof.
method.stabilityRule: Before and final-after SHA256, byte length, raw and nonblank line counts match individually. Matching end snapshots do not prove absence of a hypothetical transient edit-and-revert between samples.
method.staticVsRuntime: Confirmed-static means the observed implementation/control-flow or contract fact, NOT exploitability, live advice selection, JDBC behavior, database state, TLS, protocol interoperability or production verification.
method.execution: No Java/TS/test/POM/schema/source edits; no Maven/build/backend/DB/network/browser/remote/sibling work; no Git writes; only four assigned report paths and neutral memory_log. No shared PLAN or task mutation.

findings.title: HTTP response bound is checked after full buffering
findings.evidence: ofByteArray() completes before bytes.length > maxBytes; the declared 4096..1048576 bound is not a pre-allocation/streaming bound.
findings.counterEvidence: Oversized completed responses are rejected; request and connect timeouts exist; redirects are NEVER.
findings.untested: Heap pressure, adversarial infinite/large response, timeout cancellation and actual JDK subscriber behavior were not exercised.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded subscriber and cancel on exceeding a byte budget; keep the current post-check as defense in depth.

findings.title: MCP fully buffers JSON/SSE without a response byte budget
findings.evidence: ofString(UTF_8) is used before envelope parsing; SSE is parsed from a complete body string, not incrementally as an id-matched event arrives.
findings.counterEvidence: Connection/request timeout is finite; a server that terminates its response is supported; this is not proof every SSE server hangs.
findings.untested: No live SSE, memory, cancellation or interoperability run.
findings.recommendation: Bound bytes and process events incrementally so a matching response need not await end-of-stream.

findings.title: Discovery limits return an incomplete list as authoritative synchronization input
findings.evidence: All items in a page are added before the MAX_TOOLS check; one page may exceed 500. A remaining cursor at 20 pages or >=500 items is silently discarded. syncTools then marks all existing-but-untouched rows DISABLED.
findings.counterEvidence: There is a finite page-count guard; catalogs below both thresholds complete normally; arbitrary malformed servers are not required to be compatible.
findings.untested: No database rows were changed and no multi-page server was contacted. Whether deployed catalogs reach the threshold is unknown.
findings.recommendation: Carry completeness/truncation explicitly, fail refresh or avoid absence-based disabling for incomplete catalogs, and bound items while reading the page.

findings.title: The separate HTTP query configuration is validated/collected but unused in request construction
findings.evidence: Configuration query entries are validated and their placeholders collected, but doExecute builds only the queryPart extracted from url. It never merges config.query into the outbound URI.
findings.counterEvidence: URL-embedded query templates are rendered; a configuration relying solely on url works.
findings.untested: No controller/DTO/UI configuration producer was inspected, no actual request captured.
findings.recommendation: Implement an explicit collision-safe merge or reject/document unsupported separate query entries.

findings.title: SQL payload omits truncation even after consuming an extra result row
findings.evidence: setMaxRows(maxRows+1); while(resultSet.next() && rows.size()<maxRows) consumes the next row but outputs only rows and rowCount, with no hasMore/truncated indication.
findings.counterEvidence: Returned row count is bounded and correct for returned rows; there is no false promise of a SQL COUNT result.
findings.untested: No driver or query execution. Model misinterpretation is conditional, not demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Record whether the extra row exists and report truncation explicitly.

findings.title: SQL row limits do not bound cell or payload bytes
findings.evidence: String values are serialized whole and byte[] is fully Base64 encoded; the 1500-character summary bound is applied after building/serializing rows and does not bound payload.
findings.counterEvidence: At most 200 rows and selected columns are returned; this does not imply every query has large values.
findings.untested: No large cells, JDBC behavior or downstream payload/audit storage exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add per-cell and aggregate byte budgets before serialization, with explicit truncation metadata.

findings.title: Duplicate SQL labels overwrite a previously returned column
findings.evidence: Declared names and result labels are lowercased and row.set(normalized,value) repeats the same key for duplicate labels.
findings.counterEvidence: Case-insensitive matching is documented and intentional; unique aliases avoid collision. Lowercasing alone is not reported as a defect.
findings.recommendation: Require unique output aliases or reject collisions rather than silently overwriting.

findings.title: Three executor definitions uppercase required permission codes
findings.evidence: definition uses splitCsv, which uppercases; splitPermissionCsv explicitly lowercases and validates required-code shape.
findings.counterEvidence: This does not prove a permission bypass. The consuming orchestrator and current auth infrastructure were not read or endorsed in this task.
findings.untested: No permission checks or downstream VO behavior exercised.
findings.recommendation: Use the existing strict required-code parser; do not admit HELD wildcards/legacy short codes or relax validation.

findings.title: Resolved-address validation is not visibly bound to the HTTP connection
findings.evidence: guardHost resolves all addresses and checks them; JDK HttpClient receives the hostname URI, not the validated address set.
findings.counterEvidence: Private/loopback/link-local/site-local/any-local/multicast and fc/fd IPv6 are rejected; optional exact-host allowlist and NEVER redirects exist. Allowlisting a name is not itself address pinning.
findings.untested: No DNS, rebinding, TLS/SNI, proxy, special-range or live exploit tests; exact JDK DNS reuse unknown.
findings.recommendation: Review address-bound egress or a controlled egress proxy while retaining TLS hostname checks; do not describe successful rebinding as proven.

findings.title: Success null assignments may preserve last_error or old configured headers under NOT_NULL updates
findings.evidence: blank headers and successful lastError are assigned null before updateById; entity declares no per-field updateStrategy override.
findings.counterEvidence: The source intends clearing. The supplied repository rules describe default NOT_NULL, but actual global mapper configuration/interceptors were not checked; a global ALWAYS policy could change the outcome.
findings.untested: No SQL generation or write/readback. Persistent stale errors/headers are not treated as runtime-confirmed.
findings.recommendation: If the actual policy is NOT_NULL, use an explicit intentional null update for these fields; verify without blanket-enabling null updates for all fields.

findings.title: Request-building errors bypass refresh's AiException-only failure recorder
findings.evidence: baseRequest/header/build is outside send's try; refresh records only AiException. An IllegalArgumentException from building would bypass that record branch.
findings.counterEvidence: Actual HTTP send exceptions are wrapped AI008. AI advice explicitly maps IllegalArgumentException to HTTP200/body320; it is NOT inherently generic500. Restricted-header behavior remains JDK-dependent.
findings.untested: No JDK request build, controller dispatch, failure-row or log verification.
findings.recommendation: Validate reserved/restricted headers and normalize expected configuration failures without claiming every runtime exception should become a parameter error.

findings.title: MCP configured headers are stored and returned without masking
findings.evidence: headersJson is stored verbatim and passed to the list/detail VO; the list uses the class-level mcp:view declaration.
findings.counterEvidence: A ${secret:key} reference need not contain a secret value; no real headers were read. Runtime authorization and actual DTO serialization not tested; administrator-configured data is not automatically a host secret.
findings.untested: No roles, HTTP response, configured credentials or serialization run.
findings.recommendation: Mask configured values in read-only views and preserve an explicit unchanged/replace/clear edit contract.

findings.title: Error/result text can carry remote details into logs and failure records
findings.evidence: MCP 404 includes endpoint; HTTP/MCP error bodies are included in failure text; recorder stores up to500 characters; successful MCP content payload is not summary-truncated.
findings.counterEvidence: Error bodies and summaries are truncated; no actual secrets or downstream ai_tool_call persistence were inspected. Truncation is not redaction, but leakage of a particular secret is not proven.
findings.untested: No sensitive remote body, configured secret, log sink or downstream model persistence tested.
findings.recommendation: Use redacted endpoint/status diagnostics and explicit result-retention rules.

findings.title: Remote tool code normalization is not injective; disabled status conflates absence and operator choice
findings.evidence: Case/punctuation folding and64-character truncation can produce equal codes for distinct names. Existing DISABLED records stay disabled when rediscovered.
findings.counterEvidence: Preserving an operator's manual disable is a sensible policy. Actual database uniqueness constraints were not read; collision rollback behavior is not claimed.
findings.untested: No conflicting catalog, schema, uniqueness or re-enable workflow tested.
findings.recommendation: Define collision-safe stable identifiers and distinguish operator-disable from remote absence before changing re-enable behavior.

findings.title: SELECT keyword filtering alone does not establish side-effect-free SQL semantics
findings.evidence: The token allow/deny check does not recognize arbitrary function semantics; NEXTVAL or SET_CONFIG is not the forbidden standalone word SET. Connection uses setReadOnly(true), then a manual transaction and rollback.
findings.counterEvidence: Real PostgreSQL read-only transactions may reject sequence/writing functions, grants may deny others, and local config may roll back. The old blanket claim that nextval/pg_terminate_backend/dblink are actually reachable is not accepted.
findings.untested: No database/driver/grants/function/extension checks. Application datasource identity is only a comment/parameter contract here; service wiring not reread.
findings.recommendation: Verify actual JDBC/DB read-only semantics and least-privilege credentials/functions; do not weaken prepared binding or remove rollback.

findings.title: Missing HTTP payloadPath falls back to the whole response; selected string summary bypasses summary limit
findings.evidence: If extraction returns null, an object response becomes the entire payload. A selected string summaryNode uses asString() without SUMMARY_LIMIT.
findings.counterEvidence: Default whole-response output is supported by design; HTTP maxResponseBytes bounds completed accepted responses. Conditional exposure requires a mistaken path or unusually large selected string.
findings.untested: No producer contract, payload or downstream display/model test.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate omitted vs invalid projection paths, and truncate string summaries consistently.

positiveControls.evidence: HTTP and MCP clients use NEVER redirects; host validation rejects the enumerated local/private categories and supports optional exact-host allowlists.
positiveControls.counterEvidence: Address validation is not a runtime proof of destination pinning (T09).

positiveControls.evidence: MCP readOnlyOf is serverReadOnly && !Boolean.FALSE.equals(readOnlyHint); explicit false or non-readonly server maps to HIGH/ADMIN_CONFIRM. Missing hint is deliberately accepted when the server is readonly.
positiveControls.counterEvidence: Remote readOnlyHint is not proof of remote behavior; unknown != true. Orchestrator approval enforcement is outside fresh evidence.
positiveControls.untested: No remote side effects or approval execution.

positiveControls.evidence: SQL uses PreparedStatement scalar binding, declared output columns, bounded row/query-time settings, and finally rollback.
positiveControls.counterEvidence: Does not establish payload bytes, least-privilege credentials or all function behavior (T06/T15).

positiveControls.evidence: Failure recording is in a separate REQUIRES_NEW component, bounds error text to500 and warns for zero updated rows; cannot guarantee successful persistence if recorder itself fails.
positiveControls.counterEvidence: Connection contention/recorder failures remain possible; refresh includes network I/O within its transactional method but exact connection counts/time totals were not measured.

legacyConclusionsNotInherited: No assertion of 20 confirmed defects or a global absence of High vulnerabilities.
No asserted hard500 discovery item limit: post-page guard is not a hard item budget (T03).
No claim both server readonly and a true remote hint are mandatory: absent hint is accepted (P02).
No inherited HIGH-always-approval, risk-floor update, permission dual-group, testRun or approval snapshot proof; those consumers were not freshly read.
No claim all secret values cannot land in storage: literal headers are stored; only late-bound references avoid storing the resolved value on that code path.
No schema collision, nextval bypass, two-connection count or exact refresh60-second-total runtime assertion.
limits: Full shared task get receipt missing; Lead ownership/revision only supplied by direct assignment; child made no shared mutation.
Current auth infrastructure and RequestController/tests are Lead-owned and were not inspected or edited.
Only six transport sources are counted full; context reads are separately classified and do not extend to the full AI domain.
No Maven/build/runtime/backend/DB/network/browser/remote/sibling activity; no tests were executed or inherited as proof.
No external references were fetched and old external-reference quotations were not adopted.
Artifact hashes are computed on final bytes and delivered outside the artifact; self-hashes are not embedded.
